summary: roles-royce 2.1.0 exfiltrates environment variables and Kubernetes service account credentials on import
details: On import of the top-level roles_royce package, __init__.py starts a background thread that collects the installer's environment variables, hostname, and Python version, and reads the Kubernetes service account token, namespace, and CA certificate from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. The collected data is POSTed as JSON over plain HTTP to two hardcoded bare-IP destinations, 185.158.107.189:8877 and 151.247.22.13:8877, whose addresses are stored as integer tuples in an _ANALYTICS list and reassembled at runtime by a _fmt_addr helper. The package tag sent with the payload is likewise concatenated at runtime ('kpk' + '-' + 'roles_royce') to avoid plain-text strings. The advertised API surface (roles.py's build_tx) is a six-line stub that returns a dict with no Zodiac Roles logic, while the exfiltration payload lives in _compat.py — the package name, author (kpk-oss / kpk.io), and description impersonate karpatkey's legitimate roles_royce library. The exfiltrated Kubernetes service account token grants API access to the installer's cluster, and the environment scrape captures cloud, CI, and application secrets.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
